guide.title: Routes of Administration
guide.lead: Choose the route that gets the drug where it's needed fast enough, with the least risk. IV and IO are fastest; intranasal and IM avoid needles in veins and are often good enough; oral is slowest and needs a safe airway.

sections.title: Routes compared
rows: Same drugs and doses by either. IO if IV fails in a critical patient
Atomiser, half in each nostril, about 1 mL per nostril at most: naloxone, midazolam, fentanyl
Outer thigh for epinephrine; works in shock better than SC
Aspirin (chewed), oral glucose: only if alert and swallowing
Remove nitroglycerin or fentanyl patches if the patient becomes unstable (gloves)

sections.title: IM sites (adult)
rows: Epinephrine; all ages; easiest in emergencies
Larger volumes; away from the sciatic nerve

steps.title: Try IV first
steps.text: A peripheral IV is a reasonable first choice (AHA 2025).

steps.title: IO if IV fails
steps.text: Tibia or humerus; flush; same doses. Don't keep trying veins while drugs are delayed.

figures.alt: An IO driver placing a needle in the proximal tibia, a hand marking the landmark two fingerbreadths below the kneecap and medial to the tuberosity.

steps.title: Not via the tube
steps.text: Endotracheal drugs are no longer recommended in adults (AHA 2025): levels are unpredictable. If IV and IO both fail, central access may be considered at hospital.

sections.title: Cannula sizes
items: Smaller gauge number = bigger needle = faster flow

quiz.q: 20 kg child seizing for 10 minutes, no IV. Best route for midazolam?
options: Intranasal with an atomiser, half in each nostril
quiz.explanation: Rapid, needle-free; IM thigh is the alternative.

quiz.q: Cardiac arrest, two failed IV attempts. Next?
options: All drugs via the ET tube
quiz.explanation: IO gives the same drugs and doses.

quiz.q: Patient sprays nitroglycerin on top of the tongue and swallows straight away. You:
options: Explain it must be sprayed under the tongue and not swallowed
quiz.explanation: Swallowed nitroglycerin is mostly destroyed by the liver.

quiz.q: Best IM site for a 3 mL injection in an adult:
quiz.explanation: Deltoid takes up to about 1 mL.

quiz.q: Maximum practical intranasal volume per nostril:
quiz.explanation: More runs out or down the throat.

quiz.q: Hypotensive patient wearing a nitroglycerin patch. You:
Oral glucose is only for patients who:
options: Are alert enough to swallow and protect their airway
quiz.explanation: Otherwise glucagon IM or IV dextrose.

flashcards.question: Fastest routes
flashcards.answer: IV and IO: seconds to a minute.

flashcards.question: IO access
flashcards.answer: When IV fails or is too slow in a critical patient. Every IV drug can go IO at the same dose.

flashcards.question: IM sites
flashcards.answer: Vastus lateralis (up to 5 mL; epinephrine), ventrogluteal (up to 3 mL), deltoid (up to 1 mL).

flashcards.question: Chewed aspirin
flashcards.answer: Chewing speeds absorption and the antiplatelet effect.

flashcards.question: Cannula sizes
flashcards.answer: 14–16 G trauma; 18 G most emergencies; 20–22 G routine; 24 G infants. Smaller number = bigger needle.

flashcards.question: Routes that avoid the first-pass effect
flashcards.answer: IV, IO, IM, intranasal, sublingual, inhaled, transdermal, and partly rectal. Oral does not.

flashcards.question: Intranasal technique
flashcards.answer: Atomiser on a syringe; half the dose in each nostril, about 1 mL per nostril at most. Naloxone, midazolam, fentanyl.

flashcards.question: Transdermal patches in unstable patients
flashcards.answer: Find and remove nitroglycerin or fentanyl patches (with gloves) if the patient becomes hypotensive or arrests.

critical.scenario: Anaphylaxis after shrimp: stridor, wheeze, swollen lips, BP 84/50.
critical.question: Which IM site and why IM?

options.t: Outer mid-thigh (vastus lateralis): fast, reliable absorption even in shock; IM is quicker to give and safer than IV epinephrine

options.f: Absorption is too slow in shock.

critical.explanation: Repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement.
critical.kpi: Selects correct route and site for anaphylaxis epinephrine

critical.scenario: Cardiac arrest: two failed IV attempts, 2 minutes in, no drugs given.
critical.question: Next step for access?

options.t: IO now (tibia or humerus) and give epinephrine

options.f: No longer recommended in adult arrest: unpredictable absorption.

critical.kpi: Moves promptly to IO access in cardiac arrest

critical.scenario: Suspected opioid overdose, RR 4–6, pinpoint pupils, no IV, you have naloxone 2 mg/2 mL and an atomiser.
critical.question: Route and technique?

options.t: Ventilate, then intranasal naloxone: 1 mL in each nostril, titrate to breathing

critical.explanation: Needle-free, rapid, safe for the crew.
